llm.summary: This skill’s website-building purpose is understandable, but its artifacts contain security-relevant inconsistencies around multi-tenant admin access and payment callback protection that users should review before deployment.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose—generate and deploy EdgeOne Pages full-stack websites—is coherent, but it includes high-impact e-commerce, payment, admin CRUD, and multi-tenant capabilities, and some included reference code does not consistently enforce the claimed tenant boundaries.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The docs describe automatic deployment and provide EdgeOne CLI/database commands. These are purpose-aligned, but they can publish a public site or mutate production databases and should remain explicitly user-approved.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec, but the README asks users to install an unpinned global EdgeOne CLI and the package includes publish/build scripts. No automatic execution is shown.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill needs JWT, database, AI, and payment-related secrets for its stated use case, but the registry requirements say no required environment variables, so users may not see the credential needs until reading the skill docs.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifacts describe persistent sessions, tenant data, admin roles, audit logs, and payment callbacks; these are expected for the app type, but inconsistent tenant filtering and callback protection create material privilege-boundary concerns.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Treat this as a powerful website-generation/deployment skill. Before using it for a real e-commerce, payment, admin, or multi-tenant site, review the generated code for tenant_id filtering on every database query, verify payment callback signature/IP handling, declare and scope all secrets, and require explicit approval before deploying or running database migrations.

evidence.explanation: The admin reference queries products without a tenant_id filter, even though the broader artifacts claim multi-tenant isolation and require all SQL to include a tenant placeholder. If generated from this reference, admin functions could read or change data across tenants.

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Before deploying, review generated admin/database code and require tenant_id scoping plus role checks on every admin CRUD, stats, order, user, and product query.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: A generated multi-tenant admin panel could expose or modify other tenants’ products, orders, users, or statistics if tenant scoping is not added everywhere.

evidence.explanation: The documentation presents payment callback IP whitelisting as a security measure, but the included middleware implementation only passes payment callback paths onward with next() and does not show an IP allowlist check.
evidence.snippet: 支付回调 IP 白名单 | Platform Middleware 直接 return

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Implement and test explicit payment-provider signature verification and/or IP allowlisting, and update the documentation so it matches the actual middleware behavior.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: Users may believe payment callbacks are IP-whitelisted when the provided runtime artifact does not implement that protection, increasing risk if downstream callback verification is incomplete.

evidence.explanation: The runtime middleware explicitly lets payment notification paths bypass normal JWT flow. Payment callbacks commonly need special handling, but the included code does not itself enforce the claimed IP whitelist or show a compensating check.

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Keep payment callbacks unauthenticated only if each callback handler verifies the payment provider signature, source, amount, order state, and idempotency before changing order status.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: Payment status-changing endpoints may be reachable without the protection users expect unless generated cloud functions independently verify provider signatures and idempotency.

evidence.explanation: The skill declares sensitive JWT, AI, payment, and database secrets in its own frontmatter, while the registry metadata says no required environment variables. These credentials are expected for the stated app type, but should be visible before installation/use.
evidence.snippet: JWT_SECRET: ... required: true ... AI_API_KEY ... WX_APPID ... WX_MCHID ... DATABASE_URL

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Declare all required and optional secrets in registry metadata and provide clear least-privilege setup instructions for each scenario.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: Users will need to provide secrets that can affect authentication, AI provider billing, payment setup, and database access.

evidence.explanation: The AI chat reference forwards chat history to an external AI API. That is purpose-aligned for an AI assistant site, but it is a sensitive data flow users should understand.
evidence.snippet: const response = await fetch('https://api.example.com/chat', ... body: JSON.stringify({ messages: history, stream: true })

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Disclose the AI provider, data sent, retention expectations, and any opt-out or redaction behavior before enabling the AI chat module.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: Chat history or user-provided content may be sent to whichever AI provider the generated app configures.

evidence.explanation: The deployment workflow asks users to install a global CLI and log in to a cloud provider. This is central to the skill’s purpose and is user-directed, but it gives deployment authority to the CLI/toolchain.
evidence.snippet:
npm install -g edgeone
edgeone login --site china
edgeone pages deploy -n my-site

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Install the EdgeOne CLI from the official source, pin or verify versions where possible, and review deployment output before publishing.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: A compromised or unexpected CLI version could affect the deployed site or EdgeOne account actions.

abnormal_behavior_control.summary: Payment callback protection is over-claimed relative to the included middleware, and deployment depends on a user-installed cloud CLI.

permission_boundary.summary: Multi-tenant isolation is claimed, but included admin reference queries lack tenant filters and could lead to cross-tenant data access if generated as written.

sensitive_data_protection.summary: The AI module forwards chat history to an external AI API as part of its expected function, which should be disclosed and controlled.
